stories.title: Midterm votes are being counted, with crypto's market bill at stake
stories.summary: Polls are closing across the US and the count for control of Congress has begun. The result shapes whether the CLARITY Act, the US crypto market-structure bill, can still pass. Prediction markets favour Democrats, but no race had been called when CoinDesk's live blog opened at 7:00pm ET (07:00 Wed Bangkok).
points: Kalshi's live markets priced Democratic control at 93% for the House and 73% for the Senate when read for this edition (about 00:00 UTC Wed, 07:00 Bangkok).
At about 4pm ET Tuesday, Forbes reported Polymarket at 95% for a Democratic House and 75% for a Democratic sweep of both chambers, with Kalshi at 72% for a sweep.
Republicans hold the Senate 53-45, with 2 independents; Democrats need a net gain of 4 Senate seats and 3 House seats, per Cointelegraph.
Cointelegraph describes the CLARITY Act as "stalled".
Most of Alaska votes until 1:00am ET (13:00 Wed Bangkok), and CoinDesk says not every race may be called by Wednesday morning.

stories.title: Binance hack report: a fake job interview opened the door
stories.summary: Binance says North Korean hackers posed as recruiters and tricked an engineer into downloading an interview "assignment", while a tampered software download hit a second engineer. Together that let them take over several wallets. North Korea denies any role. Money has started flowing back into the exchange.
points: Binance said "This should not have happened" and says it blocked 57 North Korea-linked hacking attempts in 2026, per Fortune.
The FBI blames the North Korean group TraderTraitor, and Elliptic agrees; Kim Yo Jong denied involvement through state media, per CoinDesk.
Sources differ on the size: about $6.3B stolen per Fortune citing Binance, $6.4B per Elliptic via CoinDesk. Frozen or recovered: about $2.5B per Fortune, $2.85B per Elliptic.
DefiLlama showed about $2.3B of net inflows to Binance over 24 hours, after more than $7B of net outflows on Monday, per Cointelegraph.

stories.title: Bitcoin holds near $77,000 as options traders pay up for the election
stories.summary: Bitcoin dipped to about $76,300 in the European morning on Tuesday and then steadied. US spot bitcoin funds lost about $399M on Monday, their second straight day of outflows, and options prices show traders expect bigger moves around the election.
points: Spot bitcoin ETFs saw about $399M of outflows on 2 Nov; BlackRock's IBIT lost $405M, its biggest daily outflow since June, per CoinDesk.
Near-dated bitcoin implied volatility rose to about 51% from about 43.5% the day before, per CoinDesk.
Liquidations over 24 hours rose 171% to $382.6M, per CoinDesk.

briefs.title: Wall Street groups sue the CFTC over stock perps
briefs.summary: A new trade group backed by firms including Cboe and Citadel Securities sued the CFTC, arguing the single-stock perpetual futures it cleared on Tuesday belong under the SEC, per CoinDesk.

briefs.title: SEC staff call Canton Coin a "digital commodity"
briefs.summary: A no-action letter says SEC staff will not recommend enforcement over Canton Coin's programmatic issuance; it reflects staff position, not a court ruling, per The Block.

briefs.title: Block: bitcoin gross profit halves after a Cash App fee cut
briefs.summary: Block reported Q3 revenue of $6.72B; bitcoin revenue fell 11% to $1.80B and bitcoin gross profit fell 50% to $52M, per its shareholder letter.

briefs.title: AMD tops its own guidance
briefs.summary: AMD reported Q3 revenue of $13.38B, up 45% from a year earlier, and guided Q4 revenue to about $17B, per its SEC filing.

briefs.title: Justin Sun seeks sanctions against World Liberty
briefs.summary: Sun, who invested $45M in WLFI tokens, says the Trump-linked firm disclosed UAE ties in its ownership only months into the case and now uses them to contest jurisdiction, per CoinDesk.

briefs.title: Big companies object to OKX-ICE tokenized stocks
briefs.summary: Amazon, Tesla, SpaceX and others joined objections to 24/7 tokenized versions of their shares, taking disclosed objections to 56, per CoinDesk.
